openings.claim: A revision register can carry an auditable reconciliation by recording only explicit amendment-to-superseded-row relationships. Its usefulness under missing links remains uncertain.
openings.delta: Change the carrier from manual per-batch amendment lookup to a directed replacement register. The nearest ordinary rival is manual reconciliation that checks amendment references while retaining all rows. No conversion/revision coupling is proposed.
openings.prediction: The register may reduce unsupported definite claims when a replacement is already represented under another identifier or a reference disappears. Distinguishing observations are supported resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and requests naming missing records. Equal results with greater register effort defeat the claimed advantage; no improvement is assumed.
openings.probe: Using the supplied local script or spreadsheet, prepare both variants in 35 minutes, run each against both supplied copies in 20 minutes, and freeze outputs by minute 60. Each output covers all twelve batches with a reconciled quantity or bounded disagreement, citations and at most three targeted requests. Spend the supplied extra twenty minutes comparing frozen outputs against the sealed key. Retain every duplicate and unmatched row; use only the supplied conversion table where quantities require conversion; never infer from neighboring batches. In the disturbed copy, flag the missing superseded reference and undefined status. Request their identities or definitions when indispensable; unresolved evidence remains bounded.
assumptions: Only explicit references justify replacement edges; a matching quantity or earlier effective time does not prove that the differently identified older-report row is the same replacement.
Undefined status semantics cannot be invented. Ambiguous rows remain visible and cited.
Register construction and four output sets must fit the sixty-minute review budget; the proposed allocation is unmeasured, and the cap alone does not establish feasibility.
Missing cross-report identity evidence may prevent resolution even with a register. Cycles, conflicting replacements or absent referenced rows defeat a unique replacement conclusion.
If preparation overruns, record the incomplete probe without extending the review or claiming success. No deployment or reliable performance is established.

assessment: One bounded revision-register hypothesis; supplied synthetic resources support a comparison plan, not an observed advantage. Identity evidence and reviewer capacity limit its conclusions.
